norms.heading: Civil action, procedure — admissibility of evidence, parties — default judgment may be entered, when.

path.label: Title XII PUBLIC HEALTH AND WELFARE
Chapter 210 Child Protection and Reformation

norms.text:
1. An action filed pursuant to sections 210.817 to 210.852 is a civil action governed by the rules of civil procedure. The mother of the child and the alleged father are competent to testify and may be compelled to testify. Subsections 2 and 3 of section 210.832 and sections 210.834 and 210.836 apply.

2. Testimony relating to sexual access to the mother at a time other than the probable period of conception of the child is inadmissible in evidence.

3. In an action against an alleged or presumed father, evidence offered by him with respect to a man who is not subject to the jurisdiction of the court concerning his sexual intercourse with the mother at or about the probable period of conception of the child is admissible in evidence only if he has undergone and made available to the court the results of blood tests which do not exclude the possibility of his paternity of the child. A man who is identified and subject to the jurisdiction of the court shall be made a defendant in the action not less than sixty days prior to trial by the party identifying him. Where such man is not subject to the jurisdiction of the court, the alleged or presumed father shall provide all other parties with the name and address of the man at least thirty days prior to trial. If a male witness is produced at trial for the purpose stated in this subsection, but the party calling the witness failed to implead such male witness as a party defendant or provide the notice required to all other parties, the court may adjourn the proceeding to take a blood test of the witness prior to receiving his testimony, if the court finds that the party calling the witness acted in good faith. If the court determines that the party calling the witness did not act in good faith as to the required notice, the court shall not grant a continuance, and such witness shall be incompetent to testify.

4. No party shall have a right to trial by jury. Unless a presumption applies pursuant to section 210.822, the burden of proof on all issues shall be preponderance of the evidence.

5. If any party fails to file an answer or otherwise appear in response to an action commenced pursuant to sections 210.817 to 210.852 within the time prescribed by law or rules of practice of the court, the court shall enter judgment against such party by default.

6. Copies of any paid or unpaid bill for pregnancy, childbirth or genetic testing shall be admitted as evidence without requiring third-party foundation testimony if such copies have been provided to all parties not less than seven days prior to trial. Such copies shall constitute prima facie evidence of the amounts incurred for such services or testing.
revisor_notes: Effective 7-1-97

(1998) Amendment eliminating the "right" to a jury trial did not violate the ex post facto clause, Article I, Section 13, of the Missouri Constitution. V.B. v. N.S.B. ex rel. P.M.B., 982 S.W.2d 691 (E.D.Mo.).

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 9 met à la charge de chaque partie la preuve des faits nécessaires au succès de sa prétention. Les textes du Missouri imposent surtout un soutien probatoire des allégations et prévoient une charge de la preuve pour certaines questions ou actions particulières, sans énoncer une règle générale identique.
correspondences.note_en: Article 9 places on each party the burden of proving facts necessary to prevail. The Missouri provisions chiefly require evidentiary support for factual contentions and allocate the burden for particular issues or proceedings, but do not state the same general rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe largement l’aptitude à témoigner, prévoit l’audition sans serment de certaines personnes et exclut les descendants dans certains litiges matrimoniaux. Rule 57.03 et RSMo 210.839 offrent seulement des parallèles limités sur l’audition et la compétence; aucune disposition retenue ne traite des deux dernières règles françaises.
correspondences.note_en: The article broadly governs witness eligibility, unsworn testimony by certain persons, and exclusion of descendants in specified matrimonial disputes. Rule 57.03 and RSMo 210.839 provide only limited parallels concerning testimony and competency; neither addresses the latter two French rules.

norms.text:

revisor_notes: Effective 7-1-97

correspondences.note_fr: RSMo 210.842, limité aux procédures de protection de l’enfance, permet d’imputer par jugement les frais raisonnables d’experts selon les proportions et échéances fixées par le tribunal. La Rule 68.01(a) répartit la rémunération d’un master, mais aucune de ces dispositions ne prévoit la consignation préalable d’une provision d’expertise.
correspondences.note_en: RSMo 210.842, limited to child-protection proceedings, permits judgment for reasonable expert fees in proportions and at times set by the court. Rule 68.01(a) allocates a master’s compensation, but neither provision creates a French-style advance deposit for expert fees.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffier invite les parties à consigner la provision destinée à l’expert et en informe celui-ci. Le RSMo 210.842 traite de la prise en charge des frais d’experts, mais ne prévoit ni consignation préalable ni notification par le greffier.
correspondences.note_en: The clerk directs the responsible parties to deposit the expert’s advance and informs the expert. RSMo 210.842 addresses allocation of expert fees, but not advance deposits or clerk notification.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article règle l’acompte de l’expert, la provision complémentaire et les conséquences d’une consignation insuffisante. La Rule 77.02 permet d’exiger une garantie pour les frais et d’imposer des mesures en cas de défaut; la Rule 68.01 et RSMo 210.842 concernent plus généralement la rémunération ou les frais, sans reprendre ce régime détaillé.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs an expert’s advance, supplemental provision, and the consequences of failing to deposit funds. Rule 77.02 permits security for anticipated costs and relief for noncompliance; Rule 68.01 and RSMo 210.842 address compensation or costs more generally, without reproducing this detailed regime.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge fixe la participation des parents aux frais de justice lorsqu’ils ne peuvent en assumer la totalité. Le RSMo 210.842 permet au tribunal de répartir les honoraires et frais entre les parties, mais selon un dispositif plus large et avec des exceptions propres à la procédure de protection de l’enfance.
correspondences.note_en: The judge fixes the parents’ contribution to costs when they cannot bear the total amount. RSMo 210.842 allows the court to allocate counsel fees and other costs among the parties, but under a broader scheme with child-protection-specific exceptions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe le principe d’une indemnisation de l’administrateur ad hoc, le remboursement de ses déplacements, l’indemnité de carence et le recouvrement des frais. Les textes du Missouri prévoient la fixation d’honoraires raisonnables pour le guardian ad litem et leur paiement par les parties, les fonds publics ou le comté, mais ne reprennent pas le régime détaillé des déplacements, de la carence et du recouvrement par le Trésor.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides compensation for the ad hoc administrator, travel reimbursement, a failure-to-act allowance, and recovery of the costs. Missouri provisions authorize reasonable guardian ad litem fees and payment by parties, public funds, or the county, but do not reproduce the detailed travel, nonperformance, or Treasury-recovery scheme.

path.label: Title XII PUBLIC HEALTH AND WELFARE
Chapter 210 Child Protection and Reformation

norms.text:
1. The provisions of any decree respecting support may be modified only upon a showing of changed circumstances so substantial and continuing as to make the terms unreasonable. In a proceeding for modifications of any child support award, the court, in determining whether or not a substantial change in circumstances has occurred, shall consider all financial resources of both parties, including the extent to which the reasonable expenses of either party are, or should be, shared by a spouse or other person with whom he cohabits, and the earning capacity of a party who is not employed. If the application of the guidelines and criteria set forth in supreme court rule 88.01 to the financial circumstances of the parties would result in a change of child support from the existing amount by twenty percent or more, then a prima facie showing has been made of a change of circumstances so substantial and continuing as to make the present terms unreasonable.

2. When the party seeking modification has met the burden of proof set forth in subsection 1 of this section, the child support shall be determined in conformity with criteria set forth in supreme court rule 88.01.

norms.heading: Hearings and records, confidentiality — inspection allowed, when.

path.label: Title XII PUBLIC HEALTH AND WELFARE
Chapter 210 Child Protection and Reformation

norms.text: Notwithstanding any other law concerning public hearings and records, any hearing or trial held under sections 210.817 to 210.852 shall be held in closed court without admittance of any person other than those necessary to the action or proceeding. All papers and records, other than the interlocutory or final judgment, pertaining to the action or proceeding, whether part of the permanent record of the court, are subject to inspection only by the prosecuting or circuit attorney or attorney under contract with the family support division or upon the consent of the court and all interested persons, or in exceptional cases only upon order of the court for good cause shown.

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC pose la publicité des débats comme principe, avec des exceptions légales de huis clos ou de chambre du conseil. Les règles du Missouri exigent surtout que les procès au fond se tiennent en audience publique, tandis que certaines procédures, notamment celles visées par le RSMo 210.846, se tiennent à huis clos.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC makes public hearings the general rule, subject to statutory exceptions for closed hearings. Missouri requires trials on the merits to be held in open court, while allowing other proceedings in chambers and requiring closed hearings in the proceedings covered by RSMo 210.846.

correspondences.note_fr: Un tiers peut consulter le dossier et en obtenir copie sur autorisation judiciaire s’il justifie d’un intérêt légitime. RSMo 452.395(2) admet les personnes ayant un intérêt direct et légitime à une audience de garde; RSMo 453.120, RSMo 210.846 et Rule 55.0275 encadrent l’accès aux dossiers fermés ou confidentiels, avec des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: A third party may inspect and copy the case file with judicial authorization upon showing a legitimate interest. RSMo 452.395(2) permits persons with a direct and legitimate interest to attend a custody hearing; RSMo 453.120, RSMo 210.846, and Rule 55.0275 regulate access to confidential or sealed records under different conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’avis du technicien ne peut être divulgué hors instance lorsqu’il porte atteinte à la vie privée ou à un intérêt légitime, sauf autorisation judiciaire ou consentement. Les textes du Missouri prévoient, dans des domaines particuliers, la fermeture ou le scellement des dossiers et la limitation de la copie ou diffusion de certains éléments.
correspondences.note_en: An expert’s opinion may not be disclosed outside the proceeding when disclosure would invade privacy or another legitimate interest, absent court authorization or consent. The Missouri provisions impose domain-specific sealing, closed-record, and copying or distribution restrictions, but do not establish the same general rule for expert opinions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article pose la publicité des débats, sous réserve des exceptions légales, et impose en appel la règle applicable en première instance. Le Missouri prévoit l’ouverture des procès au fond, avec des exceptions particulières, notamment en matière de garde d’enfants et de protection de l’enfance, sans reprendre la règle générale de l’appel.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes public hearings subject to statutory exceptions and carries the first-instance rule into appeals. Missouri requires trials on the merits to be open, with specific exceptions for custody and child-protection matters, but does not reproduce the general appellate carryover rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet au juge de fermer les débats pour protéger la vie privée, sur demande conjointe ou en cas de désordre. Le Missouri prévoit l’exclusion du public lorsque l’intérêt de l’enfant l’exige en matière de garde et impose le huis clos dans certaines procédures de protection de l’enfance, mais sans reprendre les trois motifs généraux.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits the judge to close hearings to protect privacy, on the parties’ joint request, or because of disorder. Missouri allows exclusion of the public when a child’s best interests require it in custody proceedings and mandates closed court in specified child-protection proceedings, but does not adopt the same three general grounds.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 436 exclut le public lorsque l’affaire est tenue en chambre du conseil. La Rule 55.29 distingue les procès en audience publique des autres actes accomplis en chambre, tandis que RSMo 210.846 impose le huis clos dans certaines procédures particulières seulement.
correspondences.note_en: Article 436 excludes the public when proceedings are held in chambers. Rule 55.29 distinguishes trials in open court from other acts conducted in chambers, while RSMo 210.846 requires closed court only for specified proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article exige un registre d'audience détaillé, indiquant notamment la composition de la formation, les parties présentes, le caractère public de l'audience, les incidents et les décisions. Les textes du Missouri ne prévoient pas ce registre général, mais règlent séparément l'inscription des décisions, les audiences publiques et certaines audiences à huis clos.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a detailed hearing register recording the judges, clerk, parties, attendance, publicity, incidents, and decisions. Missouri has no comparable general hearing register, but separately addresses recording decisions, open trials, and closed hearings in specified proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’affaire est instruite et débattue à huis clos, après avis du ministère public, et la décision est rendue hors la présence du public. Le Missouri prévoit le huis clos et des restrictions d’accès aux dossiers dans certaines procédures, mais pas selon une règle générale identique.
correspondences.note_en: The matter is heard in chambers after the public prosecutor’s opinion, and the decision is rendered outside the presence of the public. Missouri provides closed hearings and restricted access to records in specified proceedings, but not under an identical general rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose le huis clos pour l’instruction et les débats en matière de filiation, le prononcé public du jugement et une exécution provisoire seulement ordonnée. Le Missouri prévoit le huis clos de certaines actions de parenté et des audiences préalables, tandis que la règle générale ouvre les procès au public; l’exécution provisoire n’est pas couverte.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires closed proceedings in filiation matters, public pronouncement of judgment, and provisional enforcement only when ordered. Missouri provides closed parentage hearings and pretrial proceedings, while the general rule requires open trials; provisional enforcement is not addressed.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise la consultation du dossier par l’avocat, la partie et le délégué, encadre la délivrance des copies et permet d’écarter certaines pièces pour protéger la vie privée. Le Missouri prévoit l’accès des parties aux rapports, ainsi que la confidentialité et l’inspection limitée de certains dossiers, mais sans reprendre exactement ces modalités.
correspondences.note_en: The article regulates file inspection by counsel, the party, and the appointed delegate, limits copying, and permits exclusion of documents to protect privacy. Missouri provides party access to reports and confidentiality or restricted inspection of certain records, but does not reproduce these procedures exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC organise l’accès limité au dossier judiciaire par les personnes désignées et leurs avocats, ainsi que la délivrance de copies à usage exclusif de la procédure. Le § 210.846 limite l’inspection des pièces et dossiers de la procédure, sous réserve du consentement des intéressés ou d’une autorisation judiciaire.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC regulates restricted access to the court file by specified participants and their lawyers, and limits copies to procedural use. RSMo 210.846 restricts inspection of papers and records in the proceeding, subject to interested-person consent or court authorization.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose une instruction et un jugement en chambre du conseil, après avis du ministère public, selon une procédure orale. Le Missouri prévoit des audiences à huis clos dans certaines procédures relatives à l’enfant et exige l’enregistrement de certaines audiences, mais ne reprend pas l’avis du ministère public ni exactement cette procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a closed hearing and judgment, after the public prosecutor’s opinion, using oral procedure. Missouri provides closed hearings in certain child proceedings and requires a record for some hearings, but does not reproduce the prosecutor-opinion requirement or the exact oral procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article règle la consultation du dossier par le requérant et, sous autorisation judiciaire, par certaines personnes justifiant d’un intérêt légitime, ainsi que par leurs avocats. Les textes du Missouri organisent aussi un accès limité ou soumis à autorisation aux dossiers confidentiels, mais dans des matières différentes et selon des catégories distinctes.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs file inspection by the applicant and, with court authorization, by persons showing a legitimate interest, including their attorneys. The Missouri provisions likewise restrict or condition access to confidential records, but apply in different proceedings and use different categories.

correspondences.note_fr: Le conseil de famille siège hors publicité et ses membres sont tenus au secret envers les tiers. Les textes du Missouri prévoient la confidentialité de certaines réunions et dossiers ainsi que, selon les cas, des audiences à huis clos, mais ne posent pas exactement la même obligation générale de secret aux membres du conseil.
correspondences.note_en: The family council meets privately and its members owe confidentiality to third parties. Missouri provisions protect the confidentiality of certain meetings and records and allow closed hearings, but they do not impose exactly the same general secrecy duty on council members.

path.label: Title XII PUBLIC HEALTH AND WELFARE

norms.text:
1. In any action to determine child support needs and obligations for a child whose alleged father is less than eighteen years old, the parents of the alleged father and the parents of the mother, if the mother is also less than eighteen years old, shall be made joint parties and may be jointly liable for the support ordered by the court to the child until both the father and the mother reach the age of eighteen years. The court shall, based on the needs of the child, determine the amount of child support, including in-kind support being provided, to be paid by the alleged father who is under eighteen years of age and the amount of such payment which shall be paid by the parents of the alleged father, which shall not exceed the amount of the standard of need of the state's public assistance plan for one person. The court shall, based on the needs of the child, determine the amount of child support, including in-kind support being provided, to be paid by the mother who is under eighteen years of age and the amount of such payment which shall be paid by the parents of the mother, which shall not exceed the amount of the standard of need of the state's public assistance plan for one person.

2. The amount of the support payments to be paid pursuant to this section shall be determined pursuant to the provisions of section 210.841, except that in determining the amount to be paid by a father or mother less than eighteen years old or parent of such father or mother, the court shall also consider the following relevant facts:

(1) The standard of living and circumstances of the parents of the father less than eighteen years of age and the parents of the mother less than eighteen years of age;

(2) The relative financial means of the parents of the father less than eighteen years of age and the parents of the mother less than eighteen years of age; and

(3) The responsibility of the parents of the father less than eighteen years of age and the parents of the mother less than eighteen years of age for the support of other children.

3. The provisions of Missouri supreme court rule 88.01 shall not apply when a court determines the support obligation owed by the parents of a teen parent under eighteen years of age, pursuant to this section.

norms.heading: Paternity and support, setting aside of judgment, criteria — division to track cases.

path.label: Title XII PUBLIC HEALTH AND WELFARE
Chapter 210 Child Protection and Reformation

norms.text:
1. In the event of the entry of a judgment or judgments of paternity and support, whether entered in one judgment or separately, a person against whom such a judgment or judgments have been entered may file a petition requesting a circuit court with jurisdiction over the subject child or children to set aside said judgment or judgments in the interests of justice and upon the grounds set forth in this section. Such a petition may be filed at any time prior to December 31, 2011. After that date, the petition shall be filed within two years of the entry of the original judgment of paternity and support or within two years of entry of the later judgment in the case of separate judgments of paternity and support and shall be filed in the county which entered the judgment or judgments of paternity and support. Any such petition shall be served upon the biological mother and any other legal guardian or custodian in the same manner provided for service of process in the rules of civil procedure. The child or children shall be made a party and shall have a guardian ad litem appointed for the child or children before any further proceedings are had. If the child or children are recipients of IV-D services as defined in subdivision (8) of section 454.460, the family support division shall also be made a party and shall be duly served.

2. The petition shall include an affidavit executed by the petitioner alleging that evidence exists which was not considered before entry of judgment and either:

(1) An allegation that genetic testing was conducted within ninety days prior to the filing of such petition using DNA methodology to determine the probability or improbability of paternity, and performed by an expert as defined in section 210.834. The affidavit shall also allege that the test results, which are attached thereto, indicate that a person subject to the child support payment order has been excluded as the child's father; or

(2) A request to the court for an order of genetic paternity testing using DNA methodology.

3. The court, after a hearing wherein all interested parties have been given an opportunity to present evidence and be heard, and upon a finding of probable cause to believe said testing may result in a determination of nonpaternity, shall order the relevant parties to submit to genetic paternity testing. The genetic paternity testing costs shall be paid by the petitioner.

4. Upon a finding that the genetic test referred to herein was properly conducted, accurate, and indicates that the person subject to the child support payment order has been excluded as the child's father, the court shall, unless it makes written findings of fact and conclusions of law that it is in the best interest of the parties not to do so:

(1) Grant relief on the petition and enter judgment setting aside the previous judgment or judgments of paternity and support, or acknowledgment of paternity under section 210.823 only as to the child or children found not to be the biological child or children of the petitioner;

(2) Extinguish any existing child support arrearage only as to the child or children found not to be the biological child or children of the petitioner; and

(3) Order the department of health and senior services to modify the child's birth certificate accordingly.

5. The provisions of this section shall not apply to grant relief to the parent of any adopted child.

6. A finding under subsection 4 of this section shall constitute a material mistake of fact under section 210.823.

7. The provisions of this section shall not be construed to create a cause of action to recover child support or state debt, under subdivision (2) of subsection 1 of section 454.465 and subsection 10 of section 452.340, that was previously paid pursuant to the order. The petitioner shall have no right for reimbursement for any moneys previously paid pursuant to said order.

8. Any petitioner who has pled guilty to or been found guilty of an offense for criminal nonsupport under section 568.040, as to a child or children who have been found not to be the biological child or children of the petitioner, may apply to the court in which the petitioner pled guilty or was sentenced for an order to expunge from all official records all recordations of his arrest, plea, trial, or conviction. If the court determines, after hearing, that the petitioner has had a judgment or judgments of paternity and support set aside under this section, the court shall enter an order of expungement. Upon granting of the order of expungement under this subsection, the records and files maintained in any administrative or court proceeding in an associate or circuit division of the circuit court under this section shall be confidential and only available to the parties or by order of the court for good cause shown. The effect of such order shall be to restore such person to the status he or she occupied prior to such arrest, plea, or conviction and as if such event had never taken place. No person as to whom such order has been entered shall be held thereafter under any provision of any law to be guilty of perjury or otherwise giving a false statement by reason of his failure to recite or acknowledge such arrest, plea, trial, conviction, or expungement in response to any inquiry made of him for any purpose whatsoever and no such inquiry shall be made for information relating to an expungement under this section.

9. Beginning in 2010, the family support division shall track and report to the general assembly the number of cases known to the division in which a court, within the calendar year, set aside a previous judgment or judgments of paternity and support under subsection 4 of this section. The family support division shall submit the report annually by December thirty-first.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article encadre les mesures provisoires d’assistance éducative prises en urgence, l’audition des intéressés, les convocations sous quinze jours et le dessaisissement territorial. correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1200-2 fixe la compétence territoriale du juge des enfants selon le lieu de résidence de l’allocataire ou attributaire et prévoit le transfert en cas de changement de résidence. correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe la compétence territoriale selon la nature de la demande et le lieu de résidence de l’enfant ou du parent. Le RSMo 211.453 fixe surtout les personnes à convoquer et les modalités de signification, sans délai comparable ni règle sur l’avis aux conseils.
correspondences.note_en: The article specifies the hearing location and requires at least eight days’ notice to parents, custodians, placement entities, or the child, plus notice to counsel. correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1200-4 organise l’avis d’ouverture, l’information sur l’avocat et l’accès au dossier, puis la convocation à l’audience et l’audition de personnes utiles. correspondences.note_en: Article 1200-4 governs notice of commencement, information about counsel and file access, summons to the hearing, and the hearing of useful persons. RSMo 211.453, 211.462, 211.455, and 211.459 address service, notice of the right to counsel, access to reports, and hearings, but in different juvenile proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la convocation de plusieurs personnes, avec copie de la requête, au moins huit jours avant l’audience, ainsi que l’avis des conseils et du ministère public. Le Missouri exige la signification de la citation et de la requête aux parents, gardiens et personnes ayant la garde, avec des règles générales sur la remise et le délai de signification, mais sans reprendre exactement les destinataires ni le délai français.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires specified persons to be summoned with the petition at least eight days before the hearing, and requires notice to counsel and the public prosecutor. Missouri requires service of summons and petition on parents, guardians, custodians, and other relevant persons, with general service-timing rules, but differs in recipients and timing.

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC impose l’audition des parents, du tuteur, du gardien ou service, et de toute personne utile, avec une recherche possible lorsque les parents ont disparu et un sursis maximal de six mois. Le § 211.453 prévoit les personnes convoquées; le § 210.127 impose une recherche diligente, sans reprendre ce sursis.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC requires hearing parents, guardians, custodians or services, and other useful persons, with a possible search when parents have disappeared and a stay of up to six months. RSMo 211.453 identifies persons to be summoned; RSMo 210.127 requires a diligent search but not that six-month stay.

norms.text:
1. Within thirty days after the filing of the petition, the juvenile officer shall meet with the court in order to determine that all parties have been served with summons and to request that the court order the investigation and social study.

2. If, at that time, all parties required to be served with summons have not been served, the court, in its discretion, may extend the time for service if the court finds that service may be forthcoming and that the best interests of the child would be served thereby.

3. The court shall order an investigation and social study except in cases filed under section 211.444. The investigation and social study shall be made by the juvenile officer, the state children's division or a public or private agency authorized or licensed to care for children or any other competent person, as directed by the court, and a written report shall be made to the court to aid the court in determining whether the termination is in the best interests of the child. It shall include such matters as the parental background, the fitness and capacity of the parent to discharge parental responsibilities, the child's home, present adjustment, physical, emotional and mental condition, and such other facts as are pertinent to the determination. Parties and attorneys or guardians ad litem or volunteer advocates representing them before the court shall have access to the written report. All ordered evaluations and reports shall be made available to the parties and attorneys or guardians ad litem or volunteer advocates representing them before the court at least fifteen days prior to any dispositional hearing.

Le RSMo 211.455 prévoit une enquête et une étude sociale ordonnées par le tribunal, mais dans le cadre plus circonscrit de certaines procédures de protection de l’enfance.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may order any investigative measure on the court’s own motion or at a party’s or prosecutor’s request. RSMo 211.455 provides for a court-ordered investigation and social study, but in the narrower context of certain child-protection proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose l’information et l’audition des parties et du mineur, la notification des droits à un conseil et l’accès au dossier. Les textes du Missouri prévoient la notification et la désignation d’un conseil ou d’un guardian ad litem ainsi que l’accès à certains rapports et dossiers, mais dans des cadres plus limités.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires notice and hearings for the parties and child, notice of counsel rights, and access to the case file. Missouri provisions provide notice and appointment of counsel or a guardian ad litem, and access to specified reports and records, but in narrower proceedings and forms.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise toute mesure d’information sur la personnalité et les conditions de vie du mineur et de ses parents, notamment enquête éducative, examens médicaux et expertises psychologiques ou psychiatriques. Le RSMo 211.455 prévoit une enquête sociale et des évaluations, tandis que les autres textes concernent des enquêtes ou examens dans des cadres différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article authorizes inquiries into the personality and living conditions of the child and parents, including educational investigations, medical examinations, and psychological or psychiatric expertise. RSMo 211.455 provides a social investigation and evaluations; the other provisions address comparable inquiries or examinations in different procedural settings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise la consultation du dossier d’assistance éducative, la délivrance et l’usage limité des copies, les exclusions pour danger grave et la transmission au parquet. Les textes du Missouri prévoient la confidentialité et l’accès encadré aux dossiers ou rapports de protection de l’enfance, mais pas ce régime procédural complet de consultation judiciaire.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs access to the juvenile case file, controlled copying and use, exclusions for serious danger, and transmission to the prosecutor. Missouri provisions regulate confidentiality and access to child-protection records or reports, but do not establish the same complete judicial-file consultation regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1200-4 organise l’avis d’ouverture, l’information sur l’avocat et l’accès au dossier, puis la convocation à l’audience et l’audition de personnes utiles. Les RSMo 211.453, 211.462, 211.455 et 211.459 prévoient respectivement la signification, l’information sur le droit à l’avocat, l’accès aux rapports et l’audience, mais dans des procédures juvéniles différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1200-4 governs notice of commencement, information about counsel and file access, summons to the hearing, and the hearing of useful persons. RSMo 211.453, 211.462, 211.455, and 211.459 address service, notice of the right to counsel, access to reports, and hearings, but in different juvenile proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise la consultation du dossier par l’avocat, la partie et le délégué, encadre la délivrance des copies et permet d’écarter certaines pièces pour protéger la vie privée. Le Missouri prévoit l’accès des parties aux rapports, ainsi que la confidentialité et l’inspection limitée de certains dossiers, mais sans reprendre exactement ces modalités.
correspondences.note_en: The article regulates file inspection by counsel, the party, and the appointed delegate, limits copying, and permits exclusion of documents to protect privacy. Missouri provides party access to reports and confidentiality or restricted inspection of certain records, but does not reproduce these procedures exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: Le tribunal ou le juge doit effectuer ou faire effectuer les investigations utiles et peut charger le juge des enfants. Le RSMo 211.455 prévoit une enquête et une étude sociale ordonnées par le tribunal, mais dans les procédures de retrait de l’autorité parentale; les autres textes concernent des procédures différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The court or judge must conduct or order useful investigations and may assign the juvenile judge. RSMo 211.455 provides for a court-ordered investigation and social study, but specifically in termination proceedings; the other provisions concern different proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise le juge à ordonner d’office ou sur demande toute mesure d’instruction, notamment une enquête sociale ou des constatations. RSMo 452.390 et 211.455 prévoient des enquêtes et rapports dans des procédures de garde ou de protection de l’enfance; Rule 60.01 vise plus spécifiquement les examens physiques ou mentaux.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits the judge to order any investigative measure, including a social inquiry or findings by a person of the judge’s choice. RSMo 452.390 and 211.455 authorize investigations and reports in custody or child-protection proceedings, while Rule 60.01 more narrowly concerns physical or mental examinations.

2. Stenographic notes or an authorized recording of the hearing shall be required as in civil actions in the circuit court.

Le RSMo 452.395 permet d’exclure le public et de préserver le secret de certains éléments, sans imposer l’audition du mineur ni son procès-verbal.
correspondences.note_en: The judge must hear the child under article 388-1 and may hear parents or others; the hearing is private and recorded in minutes. RSMo 452.395 permits exclusion of the public and sealing of records, but does not require the child’s hearing or minutes.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose une décision au fond dans les six mois, avec une prorogation possible d’une durée maximale de six mois, à défaut de quoi l’enfant peut être remis sur demande. Section 211.459 requires a dispositional hearing within thirty days but does not impose the same overall deadline or consequence.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1189 organise l’audience d’assistance éducative : audition du mineur, des parents et des autres intéressés, observations des conseils, huis clos et avis du parquet. Les dispositions du Missouri encadrent l’audience de placement, la représentation de l’enfant et, en matière de garde, l’exclusion du public, sans reprendre exactement toutes ces auditions ni l’avis du procureur.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1189 governs the child-protection hearing: hearing the child, parents, and other relevant persons, counsel’s observations, a closed hearing, and the prosecutor’s opinion. Missouri provisions address the dispositional hearing, representation of the child, and exclusion of the public in custody matters, but do not reproduce all of these requirements.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1200-4 organise l’avis d’ouverture, l’information sur l’avocat et l’accès au dossier, puis la convocation à l’audience et l’audition de personnes utiles. Les RSMo 211.453, 211.462, 211.455 et 211.459 prévoient respectivement la signification, l’information sur le droit à l’avocat, l’accès aux rapports et l’audience, mais dans des procédures juvéniles différentes.

RSMo 211.453, 211.462, 211.455, and 211.459 address service, notice of the right to counsel, access to reports, and hearings, but in different juvenile proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose une instruction et un jugement en chambre du conseil, après avis du ministère public, selon une procédure orale. Le Missouri prévoit des audiences à huis clos dans certaines procédures relatives à l’enfant et exige l’enregistrement de certaines audiences, mais ne reprend pas l’avis du ministère public ni exactement cette procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a closed hearing and judgment, after the public prosecutor’s opinion, using oral procedure. norms.heading: Appointment of guardian ad litem or child's counsel, when — rights of parent, guardian, or counsel — county to pay court costs, exceptions.

path.label: Title XII PUBLIC HEALTH AND WELFARE

norms.text:
1. In all actions to terminate parental rights, if not previously appointed pursuant to section 210.160, a guardian ad litem or child's counsel shall be appointed for the child as soon as practicable after the filing of the petition.

2. The parent or guardian of the person of the child shall be notified of the right to have counsel, and if they request counsel and are financially unable to employ counsel, counsel shall be appointed by the court. Notice of this provision shall be contained in the summons. When the parent is a minor or incompetent the court shall appoint a guardian ad litem to represent such parent.

3. The guardian ad litem or child's counsel shall, during all stages of the proceedings:

(1) Be the legal representative of the child, and may examine, cross-examine, subpoena witnesses and offer testimony. The guardian ad litem or child's counsel may also initiate an appeal of any disposition that he determines to be adverse to the best interests of the child;

(2) Be an advocate for the child during the dispositional hearing and aid in securing a permanent placement plan for the child. To ascertain the child's wishes, feelings, attachments, and attitudes, he shall conduct all necessary interviews with persons, other than the parent, having contact with or knowledge of the child and, if appropriate, with the child;

(3) Protect the rights, interest and welfare of a minor or incompetent parent by exercising the powers and duties enumerated in subdivisions (1) and (2) of this subsection.

4. Court costs shall be paid by the county in which the proceeding is instituted, except that the court may require the agency or person having or receiving legal or actual custody to pay the costs.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose l’information du mineur discernant sur son droit d’être entendu et assisté d’un avocat, ainsi qu’une mention dans la décision. Les textes du Missouri prévoient la désignation d’un représentant ou d’un avocat pour l’enfant, mais pas une obligation générale identique d’information directe du mineur.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires an ascertainable minor to be informed of the right to be heard and assisted by counsel, with compliance noted in the decision. The Missouri provisions provide for appointment of a guardian ad litem or child’s counsel, but do not impose the same general duty to inform the child directly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit la désignation d’un avocat lorsque le mineur entendu le demande sans en choisir un. Les textes du Missouri organisent la désignation d’un guardian ad litem ou d’un counsel dans certaines procédures de protection ou de déchéance parentale, mais sans reprendre ce mécanisme ni ces conditions.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires appointment of counsel when the child requests a hearing with a lawyer but does not choose one. The Missouri provisions appoint a guardian ad litem or child’s counsel in specified protection or termination proceedings, but do not reproduce this mechanism or its conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose l’information et l’audition des parties et du mineur, la notification des droits à un conseil et l’accès au dossier. Les textes du Missouri prévoient la notification et la désignation d’un conseil ou d’un guardian ad litem ainsi que l’accès à certains rapports et dossiers, mais dans des cadres plus limités.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires notice and hearings for the parties and child, notice of counsel rights, and access to the case file. Missouri provisions provide notice and appointment of counsel or a guardian ad litem, and access to specified reports and records, but in narrower proceedings and forms.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article reconnaît aux parents, au tuteur et au mineur discernant le choix d’un conseil ou la demande d’une désignation d’office, dans les huit jours, et impose le rappel de ce droit. Le Missouri prévoit l’information et la désignation d’un avocat dans certaines procédures, ainsi que la représentation de l’enfant, mais dans des cadres et conditions différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article gives parents, guardians, and discerning minors a right to choose counsel or request court-appointed counsel, with appointment within eight days and notice of the right. Missouri provides notice and appointed counsel in certain proceedings and representation for the child, but under different proceedings and conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1200-4 organise l’avis d’ouverture, l’information sur l’avocat et l’accès au dossier, puis la convocation à l’audience et l’audition de personnes utiles. Les RSMo 211.453, 211.462, 211.455 et 211.459 prévoient respectivement la signification, l’information sur le droit à l’avocat, l’accès aux rapports et l’audience, mais dans des procédures juvéniles différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1200-4 governs notice of commencement, information about counsel and file access, summons to the hearing, and the hearing of useful persons. RSMo 211.453, 211.462, 211.455, and 211.459 address service, notice of the right to counsel, access to reports, and hearings, but in different juvenile proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article garantit à l’allocataire ou à l’attributaire le droit de choisir un avocat ou d’en obtenir la désignation d’office, avec rappel à la première audience. Le Missouri prévoit un droit à l’avocat pour le parent financièrement incapable dans les actions de déchéance des droits parentaux, et un représentant pour certains parents vulnérables, mais dans des procédures et conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article guarantees the beneficiary’s right to chosen or appointed counsel, with the right recalled at the first hearing. Missouri provides counsel for an indigent parent in termination-of-parental-rights proceedings and a representative for certain vulnerable parents, but under different proceedings and conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article règle la saisine par requête, la transmission éventuelle par le procureur, la constitution obligatoire d’avocat dans certains cas et les mentions exigées. Le Missouri encadre le dépôt et le contenu de la requête de terminaison des droits parentaux et prévoit la désignation ou l’information relative à l’avocat, sans reprendre l’ensemble de ces règles.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs filing by petition, possible transmission by the prosecutor, mandatory counsel in specified cases, and required petition details. Missouri regulates filing and petition contents for termination proceedings and provides for counsel appointment or notice, but not the full French procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article détermine les personnes habilitées à interjeter appel et fixe un délai de quinze jours à compter de la notification, également applicable au ministère public. Les textes du Missouri autorisent principalement l’appel par une partie lésée et prévoient un délai de dix jours à compter de la finalité du jugement; le counsel de l’enfant peut aussi faire appel en matière de retrait des droits parentaux.
correspondences.note_en: The article identifies who may appeal and sets a fifteen-day period from notification, including for the public prosecutor. Missouri mainly permits an appeal by an aggrieved party and provides a ten-day period from finality; a child’s counsel may also appeal in parental-rights termination proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article soumet l’appel des décisions de retrait de l’autorité parentale et de délaissement à la représentation obligatoire. Le Missouri prévoit la désignation d’un avocat ou d’un guardian ad litem et certains droits d’appel en matière de retrait des droits parentaux, ainsi qu’une procédure d’appel accélérée, mais aucun régime identique de représentation obligatoire n’est fourni.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires appeals from parental-rights withdrawal and abandonment decisions to follow mandatory-representation rules. Missouri provides appointment of counsel or a guardian ad litem and certain appeal rights in termination proceedings, together with expedited appellate treatment, but no identical mandatory-representation regime is supplied.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe le principe d’une indemnisation de l’administrateur ad hoc, le remboursement de ses déplacements, l’indemnité de carence et le recouvrement des frais. Les textes du Missouri prévoient la fixation d’honoraires raisonnables pour le guardian ad litem et leur paiement par les parties, les fonds publics ou le comté, mais ne reprennent pas le régime détaillé des déplacements, de la carence et du recouvrement par le Trésor.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides compensation for the ad hoc administrator, travel reimbursement, a failure-to-act allowance, and recovery of the costs. Missouri provisions authorize reasonable guardian ad litem fees and payment by parties, public funds, or the county, but do not reproduce the detailed travel, nonperformance, or Treasury-recovery scheme.

norms.heading: Foster parent and others may present evidence, when — notice and opportunity to testify.

path.label: Title XII PUBLIC HEALTH AND WELFARE
Chapter 211 Juvenile Courts

norms.text:
1. Where a child has been placed with a foster parent, with relatives or with other persons who are able and willing to permanently integrate the child into the family by adoption, the court shall provide the opportunity for such foster parent, relative or other person to present evidence for the consideration of the court.

2. Current foster parents or other legal custodians who are not seeking to adopt the child shall be given an opportunity to testify at all hearings regarding the child. Upon the filing of a petition concerning a minor child who is in the care of foster parents or other legal custodians, the court shall give notice to such foster parents or legal custodians of the filing, any future hearings held on such petition and their opportunity to testify at any subsequent hearings held in relation to such petition, unless such notice and opportunity is waived by such foster or custodial parent.

norms.heading: Order of termination, when issued — transfer of legal custody, to whom — alternatives to termination — power of court — granting or denial of petition deemed final judgment.

path.label: Title XII PUBLIC HEALTH AND WELFARE
Chapter 211 Juvenile Courts

norms.text:
1. If, after the dispositional hearing, the court finds that one or more of the grounds set out in section 211.447 exists or that the parent has consented to the termination pursuant to section 211.444 and that it is in the best interests of the child, the court may terminate the rights of the parent in and to the child. After ordering termination and after consideration of the social study and report, the court shall transfer legal custody to:

(1) The children's division;

(2) A private child-placing agency;

(3) A foster parent, relative or other person participating in the proceedings pursuant to section 211.464; or

(4) Any other person or agency the court deems suitable to care for the child.

2. If only one parent consents or if the conditions specified in section 211.447 are found to exist as to only one parent, the rights of only that parent with reference to the child may be terminated and the rights of the other parent shall not be affected.

3. The court may order termination whether or not the child is in adoptive placement or an adoptive placement is available for the child.

4. If, after the dispositional hearing, the court finds that one or more of the grounds set out in section 211.447 exists, but that termination is not in the best interests of the child because the court finds that the child would benefit from the continued parent-child relationship or because the child is fourteen or more years of age and objects to the termination, the court may:

(1) Dismiss the petition and order that the child be returned to the custody of the parent;

(2) Retain jurisdiction of the case and order that the child be placed in the legal custody of the parent, the division, a private child-caring or placing agency, a foster parent, relative or other suitable person who is able to provide long-term care for the child. Any order of the court under this subdivision shall designate the period of time it shall remain in effect, with mandatory review by the court no later than six months thereafter. The court shall also specify what residual rights and responsibilities remain with the parent. Any individual granted legal custody shall exercise the rights and responsibilities personally unless otherwise authorized by the court; or

(3) Appoint a guardian under the provisions of chapter 475.

5. Orders of the court issued pursuant to sections 211.442 to 211.487 shall recite the jurisdictional facts, factual findings on the existence of grounds for termination and that the best interests of the child are served by the disposition stated in the order.

6. The granting or denial of a petition for termination of parental rights shall be deemed a final judgment for purposes of appeal.

norms.heading: Application of sections 211.442 to 211.487 — what law to govern.

path.label: Title XII PUBLIC HEALTH AND WELFARE
Chapter 211 Juvenile Courts

norms.text:
1. Sections 211.442 to 211.487 apply to all proceedings commenced on or after September 28, 1985.

2. In any action for termination of parental rights pending prior to September 28, 1985, the law in effect at the time of the filing of the petition for termination of parental rights shall govern the hearing on such petition and any appeal therefrom.
